title: Kernel invariant fields in towers of curve base extensions
statement:
Let $L\subset D$ be a field extension such that $D\otimes_L T$ is a domain for every field extension $T/L$. Let $J$ be a finite group acting on $L$ and $D$ with compatible inclusion. Let $L'/L$ be finite, let $J'$ be a finite group with a surjection $\rho:J'\to J$, and let $J'$ act on $L'$ compatibly with the $J$-action on $L$. Give $D'=D\otimes_L L'$ the diagonal action $j'(d\otimes a)=\rho(j')(d)\otimes j'(a)$. Put $N=\ker\rho$ and $M=(L')^N$, and suppose $M/L$ is purely inseparable.

The algebras $D'$ and $D_M=D\otimes_L M$ are fields, and the natural embeddings identify $(D')^N=D_M$. The extensions $D'/D$ and $D_M/D$ are finite, and $D_M/D$ is purely inseparable. For a further finite group $H$ and a surjection $\beta:J\to H$, put $A=\ker\beta$, $A'=\ker(\beta\rho)$. Let $K\subseteq L^A$ and $F\subseteq D^A$ be subfields with $L^A/K$ and $D^A/F$ purely inseparable. Then $(L')^{A'}/K$ and $(D')^{A'}/F$ are purely inseparable. In particular these conclusions can be iterated through a finite tower of such group surjections and finite base-field extensions, starting with $D^A=F$ and $L^A=K$ or with purely inseparable extensions of these fields. The case $J'=J$, $\rho=1$, with a compatible action on a finite purely inseparable extension $L'/L$, is included.

All fields, extensions and purely inseparable extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. A group action here is by field automorphisms, not assumed faithful. For a subgroup $U$ acting on a field $T$, $T^U=\{x\in T:ux=x\text{ for every }u\in U\}$. Tensor product means [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication on pure tensors as above; the embeddings of $D,D_M,L'$ are the canonical ones. In characteristic zero every stated purely inseparable extension is equality.

proof.text: For $j\in J'$, compatibility on $L$ makes the proposed diagonal map respect the tensor relation: the images of $(ld)\otimes a$ and $d\otimes(la)$ are respectively $\rho(j)(l)\rho(j)(d)\otimes j(a)$ and $\rho(j)(d)\otimes j(l)j(a)$, which agree since $j(l)=\rho(j)(l)$. Additivity and multiplication are preserved on pure tensors. The map for $j^{-1}$ is its inverse, and the group law holds on generators. Thus this is an action by field automorphisms once the tensor algebra is a field. Every element of $N$ fixes both $L$ and $D$ pointwise; consequently $L\subseteq M=(L')^N$.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property and bilinearity relations; elementary check of the given compatible semilinear actions.

proof.text: Choose an $L$-basis of the vector space $M$ and extend its image to an $L$-basis of $L'$ by lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector. The latter basis has $[L':L]$ elements by def-weil-vector-space-dimension, so the former is finite. Hence $M/L$ is finite. The scalar-extension basis theorem, switching the tensor factors by $d\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes d$, makes $D'$ and $D_M$ finite-dimensional over $D$. Both are domains by the universal domain hypothesis, applied to $T=L'$ and $T=M$. The finite-dimensional-domain lemma therefore makes both algebras fields, finite over $D$. The tensor-inclusion lemma supplies the canonical embeddings of each field factor.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-tensor-kernel-inseparable-invariants with its base field $K=L$, left field $L_{\mathrm{left}}=D$, right field $M_{\mathrm{right}}=L'$, acting group $N_{\mathrm{acting}}=J'$, normal subgroup $Q=N$, and auxiliary subfield $R=D^J$. The quotient $J'/N$ has the same action as $J$ because $\rho$ is surjective with kernel $N$. All tensor-field and finite-extension hypotheses were verified in step 2. The kernel fixes $D$ pointwise, the right fixed field is our $M$, and $M/L$ is purely inseparable by hypothesis. The remaining hypothesis is the identity extension $D^J/R$. The cited equality gives $(D')^N=D\otimes_L M=D_M$ under the natural embeddings, and its next clause gives pure inseparability of $D_M/D$.

proof.text: We have $A'=\rho^{-1}(A)$ and $N\subseteq A'$. The restriction $\rho:A'\to A$ is surjective: for $a\in A$, any lift $j\in J'$ satisfies $\beta\rho(j)=\beta(a)=1$. Its kernel is $N$. Thus $A'/N$ acts on $D$ and $L$ exactly as $A$ does. Also $N$ is normal in $A'$, being the kernel of this restriction.

source.place: Remarks 2.3(iii), p.602, and §2.6, p.603: composition of equivariant alterations; agent-written field-algebra specialization using the existing tensor/two-kernel lemma. Publisher PDF read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the same tensor/two-kernel lemma with base $L$, left field $D$, right field $L'$, acting group $A'$, normal subgroup $N$, and $R=F$. Step 4 identifies the quotient action with that of $A$; the hypothesis on its left fixed field is precisely $D^A/F$ purely inseparable. Its conclusion gives $(D')^{A'}/F$ purely inseparable. Apply it a second time with left field $L$ and $R=K$. Here $L\otimes_L L'\cong L'$ by $l\otimes a\mapsto la$, inverse $a\mapsto1\otimes a$; these maps are inverse by the tensor relations and intertwine the actions since $j(la)=\rho(j)(l)j(a)$. The quotient-fixed left field is $L^A$, with the required purely inseparable extension over $K$. This gives $(L')^{A'}/K$ purely inseparable. Neither application assumes faithful actions.

proof.text: For iteration write $J_i\twoheadrightarrow J_{i-1}$, $L_i/L_{i-1}$ and $D_i=D_{i-1}\otimes_{L_{i-1}}L_i$ for the given finite tower, with the kernel-fixed-constants hypothesis at each stage. Put $A_i=\ker(J_i\to J_0\xrightarrow{\beta}H)$. Induct on $i$: at $i=0$ the assumed extensions $D_0^{A_0}/F$ and $L_0^{A_0}/K$ are purely inseparable, including the stated equality case. For the induction step apply steps 1--5 to stage $i$ with $\beta$ replaced by $J_{i-1}\to H$; step 5 gives exactly the two inductive conclusions at $i$. For every field extension $T/L_i$, scalar-extension associativity gives $D_i\otimes_{L_i}T\cong D_{i-1}\otimes_{L_{i-1}}T$, explicitly $((d\otimes a)\otimes t)\mapsto d\otimes at$, inverse $d\otimes t\mapsto(d\otimes1)\otimes t$. The tensor relations make these inverse maps, and the formula preserves products of pure tensors, hence all products by additivity. It is therefore an algebra isomorphism. Its right side is a domain by the preceding stage’s hypothesis, so the universal domain hypothesis persists and each induction step is legitimate. If $\rho$ is the identity then $N=1$ and $M=L'$, giving the stated special case. In characteristic zero the definition of purely inseparable makes all such extensions equalities.
